title: Upper Deck Seat Track Corrosion and Cabin Reconfiguration — Request for a Permanent Track Standard
abstract: Operator request for a permanent upper deck seat track standard after repeated corrosion findings under the galley and lavatory areas, and to support a nine-abreast premium cabin reconfiguration planned for 2027.

sections.request: Our upper deck floors keep coming back to us. Every time we lift the carpet in the forward part of the upper deck we find white powder and pitting along the track, worst of all under the galley and around the two lavatories. On three aircraft the seat legs would not come out without heat, and on one of them the team had to cut two track sections out and put a repair in, which took the aircraft out of the programme for nine days. We are also changing the upper deck layout in 2027 and we are not willing to put new seats onto tracks we do not trust. What we want from Aeralis is a track standard that stops this happening, not another cleaning task, and we want it embodiable during a normal C check rather than a dedicated visit.
sections.background: We first raised this with our regional support office in 2023. Since then we have recorded twenty-nine findings across five upper deck configured aircraft, and the average time between a finding and a serviceable floor is eleven days. Our own protective treatment programme has slowed the rate but has not stopped it. The maintenance provider that does our heavy checks tells us the drainage path under the forward upper deck galley is the common factor on every aircraft they have opened so far.
sections.expected_outcome: A seat track standard that survives the wet zones under the galleys and lavatories for the remaining life of the aircraft, with no repeat corrosion inspection attached to it, and a retrofit that can be embodied at the same time as the 2027 cabin change so that we open the upper deck floor only once.

type_data.business_justification: Twenty-nine corrosion findings in twenty-six months on a five-aircraft sub-fleet, an average of eleven days out of service per finding, and a cabin reconfiguration that cannot be released against the present track standard.
